text:
Sesh, the smart tmux session manager 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 

English 简体中文

 

Sesh is a CLI that helps you create and manage tmux sessions quickly and easily using zoxide.

- Smart session creation - automatically names sessions based on git repo, git remote, or directory
- Zoxide integration - jump to your most-used projects instantly
- Session configuration - define startup commands, windows, panes, and preview commands per project in sesh.toml 
- Wildcard configs - apply settings to all projects matching a glob pattern
- Built-in picker - interactive session selector, or integrate with fzf, television, or gum
- Smart URL opener - pick links from the current tmux pane and open them in your browser, with previews of GitHub issues, PRs, and pages, and bare 1234 references resolved to your repo
- Clone and connect - clone a git repo and start a session in one step
- Mkdir and connect - create a new directory (relative or absolute path) and start a session in one step
- Last session switching - seamlessly bounce between your two most recent sessions
- Root session navigation - jump to the root of a git worktree or repository
- Nerd Font icons - display session type icons in your picker
- Shell completions - tab completion for Bash, Zsh, Fish, and PowerShell

 [!NOTE]
 ⭐ If you find sesh useful, please star the repo — it helps the project grow and reach more developers!

 [!TIP]
 Want to see more features and help sesh mature? Consider sponsoring the project to support ongoing development.

 Shell Completion

Sesh supports shell completion (tab completion) for Bash, Zsh, Fish, and PowerShell. This helps you discover commands, flags, and arguments by pressing the Tab key.

 
 Bash 

 

 

 
 Zsh 

 

 

 
 Fish 

 

 

 
 PowerShell 

 

 

After setting up completion, you can press Tab while typing sesh to see available commands, flags, and arguments.

 Extensions

 Raycast Extension

The sesh companion extension for Raycast makes it easy to use sesh outside of the terminal.

Here are limitations to keep in mind:

- tmux has to be running before you can use the extension
- The extension caches results for a few seconds, so it may not always be up to date

 

 Ulauncher Extension

For Linux users using Ulauncher there are two extensions to use sesh outside the terminal:

- Sesh Session Manager
- SESHion Manager

Here are limitations to keep in mind for Sesh Session Manager:

- tmux has to be running before you can use the extension

 Walker launcher usage (Linux)

Create an action directly on $XDG CONFIG HOME/config.toml

 

 For the dmenu mode you can use:

 Fish shell:

set ssession $(sesh l -t -T -d -H walker -d -f -k -p "Sesh sessions"); sesh cn --switch $ssession

 Bash/Zsh:

ssession=$(sesh l -t -T -d -H walker -d -f -k -p "Sesh sessions"); sesh cn --switch $ssession

 For dmenu launchers replace walker -dfk with dmenu or rofi)

 Agent skill

Sesh ships an agent skill that teaches coding agents to start work through sesh instead of shelling out to tmux new-session , tmux new-window , and tmux send-keys . An agent that has it will pick a session or a window depending on whether the work belongs to something already open, resolve names and directories across tmux, zoxide, config, and tmuxinator, reuse what's already running instead of duplicating it, and leave you where you are when the work is a background step.

Install it with the skills CLI:

 

It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and dozens of other agents — skills add will ask which ones to install to, or take -a claude-code to pick.

The skill lives at skills/sesh/SKILL.md and is versioned with the CLI, so npx skills update sesh picks up changes. To install it by hand instead, copy or symlink that file to /.claude/skills/sesh/SKILL.md (or your agent's equivalent skills directory).

install.title: How to install
install.html:
Homebrew

To install sesh, run the following homebrew command:

brew install sesh
Arch Linux AUR

To install sesh, run the following yay command:

yay -S sesh-bin
Fedora (Copr)

Sesh is available from the buckaroogeek/Tmux_sesh Copr repository (Fedora and EPEL 10):

sudo dnf copr enable buckaroogeek/Tmux_sesh
sudo dnf install tmux-sesh
openSUSE (zypper)

Add the sesh RPM repository so zypper up keeps sesh current:

sudo zypper addrepo --refresh https://joshmedeski.github.io/sesh/rpm/sesh.repo
sudo zypper install sesh

The repository only hosts the latest release. To roll back, install an older .rpm from the releases page and lock it so zypper up leaves it alone:

sudo zypper install --oldpackage ./sesh_*_linux_amd64.rpm
sudo zypper addlock sesh

Run sudo zypper removelock sesh to resume updates.

Fedora / RHEL (dnf)

Add the sesh RPM repository so dnf upgrade keeps sesh current:

# Fedora 41+ (dnf5)
sudo dnf config-manager addrepo --from-repofile=https://joshmedeski.github.io/sesh/rpm/sesh.repo
sudo dnf install sesh

# RHEL / Rocky / Alma 9+ (dnf4, zoxide comes from EPEL)
sudo dnf install epel-release dnf-plugins-core
sudo dnf config-manager --add-repo https://joshmedeski.github.io/sesh/rpm/sesh.repo
sudo dnf install sesh

If you installed tmux-sesh from Copr, run sudo dnf remove tmux-sesh first.

The repository only hosts the latest release. To roll back, download an older .rpm from the releases page, downgrade to it, and lock it so dnf upgrade leaves it alone:

sudo dnf downgrade ./sesh_*_linux_amd64.rpm
sudo dnf versionlock add sesh

On dnf4, versionlock needs sudo dnf install python3-dnf-plugin-versionlock. Run sudo dnf versionlock delete sesh to resume updates.

RPM / DEB packages

Download the .rpm or .deb for your architecture from the latest release, then install it with your package manager:

# openSUSE
sudo zypper install ./sesh_*_linux_amd64.rpm

# Fedora / RHEL
sudo dnf install ./sesh_*_linux_amd64.rpm

# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt install ./sesh_*_linux_amd64.deb

Replace amd64 with arm64 or 386 as needed.

Go

Alternatively, you can install Sesh using Go's go install command:

go install github.com/joshmedeski/sesh/v2@latest

This will download and install the latest version of Sesh. Make sure that your Go environment is properly set up.

Conda

To install sesh, run one of the following commands, depending on your setup:

  • Conda/(micro)mamba users
# Replace with mamba/micromamba if required
conda -c conda-forge install sesh
  • Pixi users
pixi global install sesh
Nix

See the nix package directory for instructions on how to install sesh through the nix platform.

Note: Do you want this on another package manager? Create an issue and let me know!
